why_this_exists: Step 296 found no signal on the dashboard orders its deciles, and CLAUDE.md section 2 was rewritten to demand that measurement before anything is built. The fifteen closed families were judged before that rule existed -- mostly as top-N books or on aggregate information coefficients, neither of which distinguishes ranking skill from market beta. This asks retrospectively whether any of them had cross-sectional content the original test could not have seen.
what_this_can_and_cannot_do: It can find a family closed for the wrong reason. It cannot re-open one: a family that shows monotonicity here would need its own pre-registered test on a fresh window before it is anything more than a lead. Most likely outcome, stated in advance, is that it confirms the closures.
signals_covered: the eight price families from Step 257, plus short interest (Step 263), FINRA short-sale volume (Step 282) and Form 4 opportunistic purchases (Step 286). Families whose raw cross-sectional scores were never saved and cannot be cheaply rebuilt -- 13F linkage, PEAD/SUE, 10-K language, fractional differentiation -- are out of scope and that is recorded rather than worked around.
why_one_horizon: These families were originally tested at several different horizons. A single declared horizon makes the eleven comparable to each other and to Step 296; it also means a family that only worked at its own native horizon could be understated here. That trade is accepted deliberately and no second horizon will be tried.
multiple_testing: Eleven signals. Bonferroni at 0.05 gives a per-signal bar of 0.0045, stacked on top of every configuration already searched across 297 steps.
the_measure_that_matters: monotonicity. A signal whose deciles do not order themselves has no cross-sectional content whatever its extremes did, and unlike a significance test it does not depend on having many decisions.
